title: Memory-Tight Equivalence of AE-w and CTXT-w Notions
summary: Only the memory-tight implication from w=2 to w=3 is known; whether the AE and CTXT variants remain fully equivalent under such reductions is unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For $x\in\{\mathrm{AE},\mathrm{CTXT}\}$, do the $x$-$w$ notions for $w\in\{1,2,3\}$ remain equivalent via memory-tight reductions beyond $2\Rightarrow3$?

scope.domain: Authenticated-encryption and ciphertext-integrity security notions under memory-tight oracle-game reductions.
assumptions: The adversary's storage of the relevant message data is not treated as free.
parameters: x selects the AE or CTXT notion family
w selects the variant with value 1, 2, or 3
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the remaining equivalences among the w-variants admit memory-tight reductions beyond the known implication from w=2 to w=3.

progress.summary: The authors state that AE-w and CTXT-w are ordinarily equivalent without memory restrictions, but say it is unclear whether this survives memory-tight reductions. They identify only the w=2 to w=3 implication as memory-tight and note that other simulations appear to require remembering all prior encryption queries.
citation_labels: Ashrujit Ghoshal et al., The Memory-Tightness of Authenticated Encryption
